I've farmed this land in Quzhou for 45 years now. My two children work in the city, so it's just my wife and me handling these 8 mu. I've learned to plan carefully — with well irrigation and the wheat-maize rotation everyone here runs, I know what works. Let me think through this year.

**Winter wheat (8 mu)** — I'll plant Jimai 22 or similar improved variety in early October after the maize comes off. Last year I got about 500 kg/mu, and I don't see reason to change much. I'll apply about 15 kg/mu of urea (roughly 7 kg N) as base fertilizer along with 40 kg/mu of diammonium phosphate — that gives me the phosphorus I need and some starter nitrogen. Then I topdress another 15-17 kg N/mu at jointing in March when I can see how the crop is coming along. Total N around 22 kg/mu. That's on the higher side but fertilizer is cheaper than a lost harvest. Potassium I keep moderate, maybe 6 kg/mu — our soil here has decent potassium but I still add some. I'll irrigate four times: after sowing if dry, overwintering in December, jointing in March, and grain-filling in May. Pesticide twice — once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, once if wheat midge shows up.

**Summer maize (8 mu)** — Straight after wheat harvest in mid-June, no-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble. I use Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, good hybrids that yield well here. I'll put about 20 kg N/mu total — 8 kg as base with a compound fertilizer at sowing, then 12 kg topdressed at the big trumpet stage around late July. Phosphorus 6 kg/mu from the compound, potassium about 6 kg/mu. Two irrigations usually — one at sowing to get it up, one at tasseling if rain doesn't come. Pesticide twice: corn borer at whorl stage, maybe armyworm if it shows. Expected yield 600 kg/mu — maize has been doing better than wheat here.

The whole year I budget around 400 yuan/mu on fertilizer and 80 yuan/mu on pesticide across both crops. With wheat and maize together I pull roughly 1,100 kg grain per mu, which keeps us comfortable.
